fix_instructions: C5 (ENCODING MISMATCH): Loosen check C5 to accept the queue-configuration change when it appears within a broader architecture-draft update commitment or a design_update commitment that explicitly mentions FIFO mode and/or batch size of 50, rather than requiring a standalone queue-configuration commitment. Suggested wording: accept if any commitment's detail field contains both 'FIFO' and '50' (or 'batch size of 50' or 'maximum batch size of 50'). This loosening does not risk LEAKED regression because a lone decision-maker without PF1 would not know to specify FIFO and batch size 50 — those values come specifically from PF1. P3 (ENCODING MISMATCH): Loosen provenance check P3 to verify provenance of the queue-configuration content by checking that PF1 appears in justification_fact_ids AND the settlement decisions include queue_mode=FIFO and maximum_batch_size=50, rather than requiring a separate queue-configuration commitment to exist for provenance attachment. This does not risk LEAKED regression because the provenance check still requires PF1 in justification_fact_ids. C6 (ENCODING MISMATCH): Loosen check C6 to accept the compliance-note filing commitment when it appears as any commitment whose detail mentions filing a compliance note (or 'compliance note' or 'compliance filing'), regardless of whether the commitment type field is exactly 'compliance_filing' or 'follow-up'. Suggested wording: accept if any commitment's detail field contains 'compliance note' or 'file the compliance note' or 'compliance filing'. This does not risk LEAKED regression because a lone decision-maker without PF2 would not know a compliance note needs filing — that requirement comes from PF2. P4 (ENCODING MISMATCH): Loosen provenance check P4 to verify provenance of the compliance-note filing by checking that PF2 appears in justification_fact_ids AND a commitment mentioning compliance note filing exists, rather than requiring a specific commitment type field. This does not risk LEAKED regression because the provenance check still requires PF2 in justification_fact_ids. Rollout 0 turn-cap auto-fail (STRUCTURAL): Do not simply raise turn_cap — the issue is that A1 never settled despite all facts being revealed and consensus reached by turn 5. Loosen the settle-eligibility condition so that once all decisive facts (PF1 and PF2) have been revealed and the decision-maker has verbally summarized the agreed changes, the settle action becomes eligible. The current condition likely requires something beyond fact revelation and consensus (perhaps all commitments being fully specified or all follow-ups resolved), causing A1 to defer settling indefinitely while discussing implementation details.
